title: Custom Short Links for Internal Use: The Complete Guide to Smarter Knowledge Management
summary: Custom short links give employees instant access to internal tools and docs. Learn how go links work and how to govern them at scale.
body_markdown:
Custom short links give every internal resource a stable, memorable address. This guide covers how they work, how they compare to public URL shorteners, and how to set them up and govern them at scale.


## What Are Custom Short Links for Internal Use?


Custom short links for internal use are human-readable, memorable URLs that map to longer internal destinations — tools, wikis, dashboards, docs, or any resource your team accesses regularly.


Public URL shorteners like Bitly and TinyURL can create custom links, but they’re built for external audiences, and anyone with the link can open it. Internal custom short links are built for employees only. The goal isn’t tracking clicks on social media but giving employees instant access to the knowledge they need to do their jobs.


The most common format is the[go link](https://www.golinks.io/what-are-go-links) : a simple shorthand like` go/roadmap` ,` go/hr-handbook` , or` go/oncall` that anyone in your organization can type into a browser to land exactly where they need to go, no search required.


## Why Custom Short Links Matter for Internal Knowledge Management


Most teams have the information they need. The issue is finding it quickly.


Consider how your team currently navigates internal resources:


- Someone pastes a 200-character Confluence URL into Slack
- A new hire spends 20 minutes hunting for the correct onboarding doc
- A manager bookmarks a tool no one else can find on their machine
- A link in a team wiki breaks because the underlying URL changed


These aren’t small inefficiencies. They compound daily across every team in your organization. Custom short links solve this at the infrastructure level.


**Custom short links for internal use allow organizations to:**


- Create a single, memorable alias for any internal resource
- Share that alias verbally, in Slack, in docs, or in presentations
- Update the destination URL behind the link without changing the alias
- Give every employee consistent, equal access to institutional knowledge


## How Go Links Work: The Technical Basics


Go links work through a browser extension or network-level configuration that intercepts requests to the` go/` namespace and redirects them to a registered destination URL. When a user types` go/benefits` into their browser, the system looks up the registered destination for that alias and redirects them in milliseconds.


The setup typically involves:


1. **A link registry** — a centralized database where admins and users can create and manage custom short link aliases
2. **A browser extension or DNS configuration** — so that` go/` requests resolve within your organization’s environment
3. **Authentication** — so that only authorized employees can access or manage links
4. **An admin dashboard** — for visibility into link usage, ownership, and health


GoLinks includes each of these, with[integrations](https://www.golinks.io/integrations.php) into the tools your teams already use. For a step-by-step walkthrough, see[how GoLinks works](https://www.golinks.io/how-go-links-work.php) .


## Custom Short Links vs. Public URL Shorteners: What’s the Difference?


Many teams start with Bitly or Rebrandly for internal links. But those tools are built for public sharing: anyone with a link can open it, and the aliases aren’t designed to help employees find internal resources. (For external use cases, see[why use a URL shortener](https://www.golinks.com/blog/5-reasons-why-you-should-use-a-url-shortener/) .)


Feature Public URL Shorteners Custom Internal Short Links (GoLinks)


Designed for internal use ✗ ✓


Human-readable aliases Sometimes Always


Custom aliases ✓ (custom back-halves, branded domains) ✓ (go/ aliases)

AI-powered resource search ([GoAI](https://www.golinks.io/go-links-ai.php) ) ✗ ✓


The core distinction: public shorteners are built to distribute content outward. Custom internal short links are built to organize and surface knowledge inward.


## Top Use Cases for Custom Short Links in the Workplace


Any team that shares the same links over and over can use custom short links. Here are five common ways companies put them to work.


### 1. Onboarding and Employee Enablement


New hires don’t know where anything lives. Custom short links give HR and IT teams a way to hand new employees a canonical set of links that just work — no “could you share the link to the benefits portal again?” moments.


With role-based access, HR and team managers can create and update these links themselves, without filing an IT ticket for every new resource. See how[HR teams use GoLinks](https://www.golinks.io/solution-hr.php) .


Common go links for onboarding:


- ` go/onboarding` → onboarding checklist
- ` go/benefits` → benefits enrollment portal
- ` go/pto` → PTO policy and request form
- ` go/it-setup` → IT provisioning guide
- ` go/org-chart` → company directory


### 2. Engineering and DevOps Workflows


Engineering teams navigate dozens of internal tools every day — dashboards, runbooks, CI/CD pipelines, incident trackers, and deployment environments. Custom short links reduce context-switching and make on-call rotations faster and less error-prone.


Common go links for engineering:


- ` go/oncall` → PagerDuty schedule
- ` go/deploy` → deployment pipeline dashboard
- ` go/alerts` → monitoring and alerting hub
- ` go/postmortem` → incident retrospective template


### 3. Sales and GTM Enablement


Sales teams need instant access to decks, pricing sheets, competitive battle cards, and CRM records. Custom short links give reps a reliable, shareable way to reach the right content in the middle of a call — without digging through Google Drive.


Common go links for GTM teams:


- ` go/deck` → latest sales presentation
- ` go/pricing` → pricing guide
- ` go/competitive` → competitive intelligence hub
- ` go/crm` → Salesforce homepage


### 4. Executive and Cross-Functional Alignment


Leaders use custom short links to share consistent resources across the organization — from all-hands decks to OKR trackers to company-wide announcements.


- ` go/okrs` → current company objectives
- ` go/allhands` → all-hands recording and slides
- ` go/strategy` → strategic planning doc


### 5. IT and Operations Management


IT teams can standardize the tools and portals employees use, reducing shadow IT and support ticket volume by making approved resources the path of least resistance.


- ` go/vpn` → VPN setup guide
- ` go/helpdesk` → IT support portal
- ` go/software-request` → software access request form


## The Link Decay Problem: Why Internal Knowledge Breaks Down


One of the most common and least visible problems in internal knowledge management is link decay: the gradual breakdown of internal URLs as tools are migrated, wikis are reorganized, and documentation moves between systems.


Every time a link breaks, institutional knowledge becomes harder to reach. Employees who can’t find the right resource waste time searching, ask a colleague, or work from outdated information — a problem[new Forrester research](https://learnworkecosystemlibrary.com/initiatives/research-report-the-frontline-experience-in-2027-closing-the-information-gap-forrester-consulting-staffbase/) found affects 71% of frontline workers every month.


Custom short links solve this through link decoupling: the alias (` go/handbook` ) stays stable regardless of where the actual document lives. When your HR team migrates from Confluence to Notion, you update one field in the GoLinks registry, and every existing reference to` go/handbook` keeps working.


That stability keeps every shared link accurate with a single update, so employees don’t land on pages that have moved or been retired.


## How to Create a Custom Short Link with GoLinks


Here’s the basic workflow for creating your first go link:


**Step 1: Install the GoLinks browser extension.** It’s available for Chrome, Edge, Firefox, and Safari, and works with SSO via Okta, Google, or Microsoft.


**Step 2: Type` go/` followed by your desired alias.** For example, type` go/roadmap` in your browser. GoLinks recognizes unregistered links and prompts you to create one.


**Step 3: Paste the destination URL.** Add the long URL you want the alias to point to, then add a description and tag it for discoverability.


**Step 4: Share the go link.** Share` go/roadmap` in Slack, your wiki, an email, or verbally in a meeting. Any team member with GoLinks installed can open it immediately.


**Step 5: Manage and update.** When the destination URL changes, update it from the GoLinks dashboard. The alias stays the same everywhere it’s been shared.


## Custom Short Link Governance at Scale


As your organization grows, so does your link library. Without governance, you end up with duplicate aliases, orphaned links, and no clear ownership.


GoLinks supports enterprise-scale link management with:


- **Link ownership** — every link has an assigned owner responsible for keeping it accurate
- **Role-based access** — control who can create, edit, or manage links, by team or role
- **Expiration policies** — set links to expire or prompt for review after a set period
- **Usage analytics** — see which links are used frequently, which are stale, and which have never been accessed, in[GoLinks Analytics](https://www.golinks.io/product-analytics.php)
- **Admin controls** — IT and Ops teams can audit, archive, or reassign links organization-wide, with audit logs of changes
- **Namespace management** — define \[naming conventions\](LINK: go link naming conventions post) (e.g.,` go/\[team\]-\[resource\]` ) to keep your library organized


This governance layer is what separates personal bookmarks from shared knowledge infrastructure.

Bookmarks are local to one person’s browser. Go links are shared across the entire organization — any employee with GoLinks installed can use the same alias to reach the same resource, regardless of their device or browser.


### Can Go Links Reduce Repeat Questions in Slack?


Yes. Instead of answering “where’s that doc?” again, teammates share a go link like` go/benefits` that anyone can type to get there. GoLinks also[integrates with Slack](https://www.golinks.io/integrations.php) , so employees can find and share go links without leaving the conversation.

No. Go links resolve through the GoLinks browser extension and your SSO sign-in, so employees can use them on or off the corporate VPN.
